summary:
The frozen advisory classifier pilot used 228 distinct fresh judge conversations: 200 planned judgments on 50 historical snapshots across four requested model/effort profiles, plus 28 controls/repeats. Of the 200 primary outputs, 182 passed the strict interface; 17 exceeded prose limits and one separate controller error delivered the wrong packet. All original failures were retained without retries or relabeling. Requested launch profiles were accepted, while provider-effective configuration and independent full read-trace compliance remained Unknown. These judges classified tasks; they did not execute the historical implementations.

High category agreement is conditional on a selected cohort concentrated in bounded/complex categories. Degenerate zero-width intervals on identical retained pairs do not establish population equivalence. A labeled post hoc check of unchanged content from the 17 formatting failures changes some contrasts, illustrating complete-case selection; the wrong-input answer remains excluded. Tested semantic category controls pass, while time estimates vary. Predicted worked-time associations with historical response envelopes are modest and uncertain, and individual new predictors do not beat the pooled training-median baseline in the 12 parent-held-out comparisons. These envelopes are proxies, not verified active work.

Forty-eight of 50 tasks overlap earlier exploratory history, so this is development evidence, not independent confirmation. Keep reasoning challenge, work volume, safety and external waits separate. Judge agreement cannot establish implementing-model difficulty invariance, calibrated ability or a universal hardness scale. Preserve the full cohort, failures, controls and unfavorable results; use independent task/time/parent validation and a declared work-time or quality construct for further claims. This source finding grants no routing activation, publication, installed adoption or native operational authority.
title: Semantic classifier agreement is advisory development evidence, not execution validity
